included.note: Reaches the published source of a record the export summarises. It names no type, so it supports the lookup skills and travels only where at least one of them did.
Reads a term from corpus/glossary/terms.jsonl and the owning glossary record beside it.
Files an observation about the corpus as an issue on the repository that published it, reading corpus/manifest.json for the address. It names no type, so it travels with every bundle.

Asks the owner of a clause to accept a knowing departure from it, as an issue on the repository that published the corpus holding that clause. It names no type, because a clause reaches it from a lookup skill, so it travels only where at least one of them did.

Sends a question with no known place to the lookup skill for its type, and reads corpus/deviations/, corpus/reports/ and corpus/runbooks/ through the reference files beside it where the export carries them. It needs no type of its own, so it supports the lookup skills and travels only where at least one of them did.
Reads a control from corpus/controls/ and says what checks a rule. A control declares no part, so there is no flat file and the record is the unit.

Reads a fix from corpus/fixes/ and says whether this problem has been solved here before. A fix declares no part, so there is no flat file and the record is the unit. Where no fix matches, or something is broken now, it reads corpus/runbooks/ through ask-the-corpus/runbooks.md.
Reads a clause from corpus/policies/clauses.jsonl and the owning policy beside it.
Reads a process from corpus/processes/ and hands the steps to corpus-retrieval, because a process export carries the trigger and not the order.
Reads a rule from corpus/standards/rules.jsonl and the owning standard beside it.

Reviews a change in a forked subagent against views/review.md, read whole. It takes a rule's link from corpus/standards/rules.jsonl, and reads a control from corpus/controls/ where the export carries controls.
Generated by kac bundle from corpus/standards/rules.jsonl: every standard rule by title, under its standard's id and status, so a session about to write code can tell which rules to read.

Generated by kac bundle from corpus/standards/ and corpus/controls/: each standard rule's obligations and the controls checking it, for a reviewer to read in full. A corpus exporting no controls still gets it.

A SessionStart hook printing the breadcrumb rendered beside it, so a session learns the glossary is here before it has a term to look up. A PreToolUse hook printing the build index once a session, at its first tool call, where views/build-index.md survived. Both travel with the glossary, so a corpus exporting standards and no glossary ships neither.
